analysis.title: Vontier Corp. (VNT): 3Q26 takeaways: Raising estimates to reflect 3Q beat and improved outlook
key_insights: VNT reported 3Q26 adj. EPS of $0.92 vs GS/Visible Alpha consensus of $0.84/$0.84, a beat. Segment EBIT was +11%/+10% above GS/VA consensus.
Organic sales growth was +5.7% (GS est +5.6%). By segment MT/RS/EF&S grew +2.2%/-1%/+13.1% vs GS est +6%/+0.5%/+7%, so the beat came from EF&S (+13%) and margins, not MT or RS volume.
MT margin was 25.9%, up 740bps, a main driver of the segment EBIT beat.

Management flagged emerging supply chain constraints and memory chip cost headwinds. It plans to offset them with ongoing self-help and an estimated $10 mn incremental carry-forward benefit into next year from its accelerated structural cost-reduction program.
Management now expects FY26 operating margins to expand +180 bps, vs +100 bps prior.
VNT expects its convenience retail and fleet end markets (~80% of the portfolio) to grow 4-5% heading into 2027, as large operators execute multi-year capital investment plans.
VNT raised its FY26 adj. EPS guide to $3.60-3.64 from $3.45-3.55, with organic growth of +3% at the midpoint. 4Q26 EPS guide is $0.99-$1.03 with organic growth of +3%.
GS raises FY26/FY27/FY28 EPS to $3.60/$3.95/$4.25 from $3.50/$3.75/$4.05. Rating stays Neutral because GS sees better risk/reward elsewhere in its coverage.
GS raises its 12-month price target to $42 from $37, based on 9.5x (vs 9x prior) Q5-Q8 EBITDA. Price was $39.90 at the 5 Nov 2026 close, implying 5.3% upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised the target from $37 on a 3Q beat and improved outlook, with the multiple moving to 9.5x from 9x Q5-Q8 EBITDA. It stays Neutral on better risk/reward elsewhere in coverage.

risk_factors: Upside risks: accretive M&A, better growth in the core business.
Downside risks: growth disappoints, accelerated EV adoption.
Emerging supply chain constraints and memory chip cost headwinds, per management.
